That declaration is RETIRED by D-PR-24, user-ratified 2026-08-05 ('arm MATIF, smoke the exact command before first fire'). Its reasoning is retained below as history, verbatim where it still holds and corrected where the arm proved it wrong -- the retire is the point, not the erasure.
decision: D-PR-24. The Euronext/MATIF capture + silver legs are ARMED, and they are armed INSIDE configs/silver/dags/futures_eod_free.json rather than as a schedule of their own. This file survives its own retirement because the thing it now declares is still an ABSENCE: there is no top-level configs/silver/dags/futures_eod_browser.json, no rendered futures_eod_browser input, no futures_eod_gate._DAG_SCHEDULES entry and no dag_schedules.auto.tfvars.json entry -- and there never will be. why_folded_rather_than_its_own_schedule.the_d_pr_23_objection: 'its OWN descriptor and its OWN cron. Folding it into futures_eod_free would violate this leg's cadence contract for ~7 months of the year: the contract is stated in CET-local terms (fire AFTER the ~18:30 CET publish and BEFORE local midnight) while the default as_of_date is UTC-today, and a 22:30Z fire is 00:30 CEST in summer.'
why_folded_rather_than_its_own_schedule.why_it_does_not_hold: It measured the wrong midnight. The producer's --as-of-date defaults to datetime.now(timezone.utc).date() and the raw key's as_of_date= segment is the leg's ONLY trade-date authority, so the date the capture is filed under rolls at 00:00Z -- not at 00:00 local Paris time. The window is therefore a UTC statement: after the settlement publish (~18:30 Paris = 16:30Z under CEST, 17:30Z under CET) and before 00:00Z. A 22:30Z Wednesday fire clears the publish by 5-6 hours and files Wednesday's session under as_of_date=Wednesday, in summer and in winter alike. The CET-local framing was never the contract the code implements.
why_folded_rather_than_its_own_schedule.what_it_bought: One cron for one table. The five free venues share one table, one contract, one partition scheme, one census baseline and one gate; a second schedule would have needed a second rolling census, and the two would have read each other's rows as unexplained drift -- the same argument futures_eod_free.json's own gate_baseline_uri_note makes for keeping the four together.
why_folded_rather_than_its_own_schedule.residual_seam_carried_forward: retry.maximum_event_age_in_seconds is 86400, so a RETRIED fire may execute after 00:00Z and file the session under the next UTC date. This is the one leg with no independent date authority to cross-check (JSE reads its session date from inside the sheet; CZCE and MIAX from a venue-chosen key segment), so nothing downstream can detect it. Narrowing this chain's event age, or teaching the producer to derive --as-of-date from <aws.scheduler.scheduled-time>, is the durable fix and is NOT carried by the arm.

arming_gate.name: Euronext SETTL. semantics
arming_gate.status: RESOLVED 2026-08-05, and the resolution is what unblocked D-PR-24.
arming_gate.question: does the rendered live.euronext.com quote table's SETTL. column carry TODAY's settlement after the ~18:30 CET publish, or the PREVIOUS session's?
arming_gate.answer: TODAY's. The evening scrape reads the same session's settlement, so there is no T-1 risk and CONTRACT_MAP's settle_kind='settlement' stands as pinned for all three MATIF slugs.
arming_gate.why_it_blocked: RETAINED AS HISTORY. settle_kind='settlement' was pinned on the strength of a probe that had never been run, while the plan record stated the intraday SETTL. column carried the PREVIOUS settlement. The rendered table publishes NO DATE anywhere in its DOM, so trade_date comes only from the raw key's as_of_date. Had SETTL. been T-1 at capture time the whole leg would have been silently off by one session with NO downstream check able to detect it: not the row floors, not the census diff, not freshness, not the gate.

orphan_raw_objects.disposition: RETAIN. Do not delete. They are now ALSO reachable by an unbounded --mode backfill run, which is a deliberate consequence, not an accident.
orphan_raw_objects.what_they_are: the W1c one-shot proof capture -- one rendered table.html per product (EBM-DPAR / EMA-DPAR / ECO-DPAR). They are the measurement the EURONEXT row floors were counted from (tests/fixtures/w1c/capture_notes.md).
orphan_raw_objects.why_retain: they are evidence: deleting them would destroy the provenance of the row floors.
orphan_raw_objects.reachability_under_the_arm: the SCHEDULED task is --mode incremental --lookback-days 5, whose --since window excludes 2026-07-29, so the nightly chain does NOT pick them up. A hand-run --mode backfill would, and that is now a legitimate operation rather than the off-by-one hazard D-PR-23 named -- probe S3 resolved the settlement semantics those three captures were dated under.
orphan_raw_objects.detector_note: the 'raw present, silver absent' state under the source=euronext prefix is no longer the declared steady state. After the first fire, raw-without-silver on this prefix is a REAL stall and should be flagged.

serving_disposition.summary: UNCHANGED BY THE ARM, then FLIPPED 2026-08-20 as its own decision. Between 2026-08-05 and 2026-08-20 every MATIF lookup declined honestly (and declined rather than errored); since the flip a MATIF ask on or after the 2026-08-06 floor is ANSWERED with the per-delivery-month settle, and one before it still declines -- naming the floor instead of raising.
serving_disposition.mechanism: PRICE_COVERAGE_START (src/leviathan/silver/futures_eod_contracts.py) is the seam. WHILE ABSENT: coverage_start_for() raised ValueError rather than defaulting; leviathan.graphrag.numbers.agent.futures_eod_route caught that ValueError and returned ('uncovered', None); the executor saw a route in FUTURES_EOD_COVERAGE_CLASSES and returned status='declined' with the verbatim scope_note BEFORE ANY SQL COMPILED, so the raise never reached a caller. NOW PRESENT (2026-08-06 for all three slugs): coverage_start_for() returns the floor and covers() decides -- serve on/after it, straddle across it, and 'legacy' before it which becomes 'uncovered' because MATIF is not one of the continuous card's 12 unit_overrides. No route code changed; only the map did.
serving_disposition.separability: this is why arm and flip were two independently gateable decisions, and the arm is the proof: MATIF rows landed in silver_futures_eod for two full weeks and every MATIF answer stayed BYTE-IDENTICAL until PRICE_COVERAGE_START gained an entry. silver_futures_eod is also absent from configs/graphrag/numbers/cascade_map.yaml, so landing rows perturbs no C002 vocabulary check either -- contract_check's slug and country families iterate MAPPED causal legs, and this table has none.
serving_disposition.flip_is_a_separate_decision: adding a PRICE_COVERAGE_START entry is the FLIP. It was NOT carried by D-PR-24's arm and NOT unlocked by probe S3; it was its own reviewed change, EXECUTED 2026-08-20 by owner word after two clean weeks of nightly fires (measured on the canonical bytes: french_wheat_matif 108 rows, french_maize_matif 90, french_rapeseed_matif 90, trade_dates 2026-08-06..2026-08-19 continuous, zero red fires). The floor is the FIRST BANKED TRADE DATE (2026-08-06), never the arm date and never the 2026-07-29 orphan captures, which were never promoted to canonical. Two eval rows and the unit assertions that encoded the decline were re-keyed in the same change and now assert BOTH directions.

freshness_blindspot.statement: family-level freshness CANNOT see a MATIF-only stall, and the arm does not change that.
freshness_blindspot.why: silver_freshness_slas['futures_eod'] is the ONLY SLA for the family and freshness reads the newest canonical object across the whole family. Four healthy legs keep the clock fresh regardless of what MATIF does.
freshness_blindspot.under_the_arm: rows land that NOTHING READS (the flip is separate), so a leg that stops writing is invisible to every consumer-side check; the per-source row floor and the gate census are the only detectors.
freshness_blindspot.owner: per-leg freshness granularity is D-EI-12 / R7's. Reference it; do not fork it here.

row_floors.source_of_truth: EURONEXT_MIN_ROWS in src/leviathan/transforms/raw_to_bronze/euronext_eod.py and _MIN_SILVER_ROWS_PER_DAY_EURONEXT in jobs/batch/futures_eod_task.py. The numbers above are a MIRROR for readability and are pinned to those two by test.
row_floors.hazard: three independent hard-fail surfaces per fire, all alarming. A legitimate venue delisting of a single expiry (which the code correctly treats as a code change) REDS the leg until a human re-counts and re-pins.
row_floors.runbook: D-PR-23 required this be decided BEFORE the arm rather than discovered after, so: on a red, re-count the RENDERED table for the failing product and confirm the expiry is genuinely delisted (an expiry that reappears the next session was a truncation, not a delisting). Only then re-pin EURONEXT_MIN_ROWS in the transform. The floor is NEVER lowered to make a capture pass -- that is the one move that converts this detector into decoration.

The per-day silver floor of 24 is calibrated against a 32-row three-product day precisely so that losing one product reds the leg; an EBM-only arm would need a different floor, and the two unprobed products are guarded by their own MEASURED per-product ready checks anyway.
